definition_of_done: Every task below is done, or awaiting-human with its evidence file present, and the go/no-go gate in PRODUCTION.md returns GO on a rehearsal workspace.

classes.auto: The agent can complete this alone. Gate must exit 0.
classes.human-gated: The agent prepares the artefact; a named person signs it. Stays awaiting-human until the evidence file exists.
classes.human: Only a person can do it. The agent may draft support material but must never mark it done.

tasks.title: Record delivery confirmation as a chained event
tasks.why: Nothing moves a draft from queued to sent, so the "confirmed sent" metric can never be non-zero and the log cannot prove anything arrived.
tasks.accept: A new chained entry type DELIVERY_CONFIRMED records who confirmed, when, and the send_id it refers to; DispatchLog status changes only through it; metrics reports confirmed vs queued; a golden fixture covers both statuses; no existing chain head changes for logs that never confirm.
tasks.gate: cargo test --locked delivery && cargo test --locked golden

tasks.title: Prove backup and restore on a fresh directory
tasks.why: backups/ exists and dispatch snapshots into it, but no restore has ever been executed; an untested backup is not a backup.
tasks.accept: scripts/restore-drill.sh seeds the fixture, takes a backup, restores into an empty directory, and asserts log verify, verify-signatures and the fixture fingerprint all match; it prints the timings it measured.

tasks.title: Write the key custody and rotation procedure
tasks.why: Identity is an Ed25519 keyfile at 0600 with no documented holder, rotation path, or meaning of a lost key.
tasks.accept: docs/key-custody.md names who holds which key, where it lives, how to rotate without invalidating old signatures, what verify-signatures reports after rotation, and what a lost key costs.
tasks.gate: test -s docs/key-custody.md && grep -q '^## Holders' docs/key-custody.md && grep -q '^## Rotation' docs/key-custody.md && grep -q '^## Loss' docs/key-custody.md && grep -q 'verify-signatures' docs/key-custody.md

tasks.title: Generate the access review for signature
tasks.why: An auditor asks who could sign what, on which date. The registry answers the first half; only an owner can attest the second.
tasks.accept: docs/access-review.md is generated from `ledger operator list` plus the registry file, lists every operator, role and key fingerprint, has a review date and a signature block, and is signed off by the registry owner.

tasks.title: Schedule chain verification with an alarm that fires
tasks.why: Corruption is currently discovered when someone happens to run the command. A pilot needs it discovered by a schedule.
tasks.accept: scripts/verify-chain.sh verifies a workspace and exits non-zero on any tamper, tear or signature failure; a workflow runs it daily against a restored copy; docs/monitoring.md says who is paged and what they run first; the script's failure path is exercised by a test.

tasks.title: Rehearse retention purge and get it signed
tasks.why: purge tombstones dispositions and rosters but keeps the send log, and Legal has not seen that distinction on real-shaped data.
tasks.accept: evidence/purge-rehearsal.txt holds the dry-run output on a copy of the fixture, the exact list of what is tombstoned and what is retained, and an APPROVED line signed by Legal with a date.

tasks.title: Complete the seven human acts for a real pilot
tasks.why: The tool records legal acts; it cannot perform them. The checklist is 0/13 and every remaining task is a person's signature, decision or mailbox.
tasks.accept: ledger status reports 13/13 signed, each by a named person: privacy opinion, approval workflow, monitored mailbox, disposition form, gate copy, comparative paragraph, templates, playbook, ATS export mapping, send log, gate-blocking protocol, pilot execution, metrics, go/no-go.

tasks.title: Emit --json from every command
tasks.why: 11 of 25 commands print prose, so no runbook, dashboard or monitoring script can consume them.
tasks.accept: Every top-level command accepts --json and emits one object on stdout with no prose; a contract test enumerates the clap commands and fails if any lacks the flag; README documents the shape of each.

tasks.title: Write the incident runbook
tasks.why: Today the first responder would have to read this repository at 2am.
tasks.accept: docs/incident-runbook.md covers torn tail, failed verification, lost key, wrong disposition, hostile reply and a data-subject request, each with the first three commands, the decision owner and the evidence to keep.
tasks.gate: for s in 'torn tail' 'verification' 'lost key' 'wrong disposition' 'hostile reply' 'data-subject'; do grep -qi "$s" docs/incident-runbook.md || exit 1; done

tasks.title: Prove the 24-hour escalation SLA is covered
tasks.why: policy.json names an owner and 24 hours; nobody has answered a test message.
tasks.accept: evidence/oncall-test.txt records a test reply sent to the monitored mailbox, the time to first response, the named backup, and the dates each person is covering.

tasks.title: Cut and verify release v0.1.0
tasks.why: release.yml exists but no tag has been pushed, so there is no downloadable artefact with checksums an auditor can keep.
tasks.accept: Tag v0.1.0 builds three targets, uploads tarballs with SHA-256, ships verify_log.py, FORMAT_SPEC.md and THREAT_MODEL.md inside, and the release notes name the test count and the fixture head.
tasks.gate: gh release view v0.1.0 --json tagName,assets --jq '.assets | length > 0'

tasks.title: Drill the data-subject request path
tasks.why: "What do you hold about me?" has a different answer for unchained state than for the send log, and nobody has walked it.
tasks.accept: scripts/dsar-drill.sh runs find --hash, purge --dry-run and a log export against the fixture, prints what is erasable and what is only deletable with the workspace, and docs/dsar.md states the answer in one page.

tasks.title: Version every state document, not just the send log
tasks.why: A workspace from an older build is currently indistinguishable from a corrupt one.
tasks.accept: Every JSON state file carries schema_version; migrate reads each older version and writes the current one; a test per version proves refusal on unknown and upgrade on known.

tasks.title: Add the three properties as proptest suites
tasks.why: The invariants are covered by examples, not by generated input; a chain that only survives hand-written cases is not evidence.
tasks.accept: proptest suites assert no send without a disposition, a chain that stays linked under arbitrary appends, and supersede never rewriting history; they run in CI in under a minute.

tasks.title: Generate the audit evidence pack
tasks.why: An auditor should read one directory in ten minutes, not ask six questions.
tasks.accept: scripts/evidence-pack.sh collects anchors, verify output, purge reports, access review, restore drill log and the release checksums into evidence/<date>/ with an index.json naming each file and its digest.

tasks.title: Close the accessibility findings on the preview
tasks.why: The checker still reports no skip link and sub-44px controls in the footer at 320.
tasks.accept: A skip link is the first tab stop on every route and is visible on focus; every link and control outside running text is at least 44px at 320 and 390; the checker's skip-link, focus-ring and tap-size checks pass.
tasks.gate: cd web && bun run test && bun run lint

tasks.title: Turn on branch protection and required checks
tasks.why: main deploys production and accepts a force-push today.
tasks.accept: main requires test, msrv, web, supply-chain and coverage; force-push and deletion are off; the owner has signed the change record.

tasks.title: Automate dependency updates behind the same gate
tasks.why: cargo-deny and the MSRV job exist, but nothing brings updates forward, so the tree ages until it is a project. The workflow can land before branch protection is on; the PRs it opens are gated by CI either way.
tasks.accept: A scheduled workflow opens one grouped PR for cargo and one for bun; both are gated by the existing CI; deny.toml is untouched.

tasks.title: Record the design-gate decision once
tasks.why: The landing carries 30 open tasteskill findings; they are the hanging-margin design and the missing kit grid. Re-litigating them each review costs more than deciding.
tasks.accept: evidence/design-decision.md states accept-with-reason or port-to-kit, lists the failing checks it covers, and is signed by the product owner.
